stories.title: Ex-Bosnian Serb military leader Ratko Mladic dead at 84
stories.summary: Bosnian Serb general Ratko Mladic, who was serving a life sentence for war crimes committed during Bosnia's 1992-95 war has died, a United Nations official said. Serbian state broadcaster RTS reported on Thursday that he died in a prison hospital in the Hague, after suffering several strokes. A family member of Mladic, who spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the situation, confirmed the reports to the Associated Press and said Mladic's son, Darko Mladic, was on the way to the Hague. The International Criminal Court for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) convicted Mladic of charges including crimes against humanity and genocide in 2017, handing him a life sentence. The verdict was confirmed on appeal in 2021. Mladic was held responsible for his role in the 1992 to 1995 war in Bosnia, including July 1995 massacre of some 8,000 Muslim men and boys at Screbrenica. The slaughter, the worst single atrocity in Europe since World War II, saw him named the "Butcher of Bosnia." Under Mladic's command, Bosnian Serb forces besieged Sarajevo and other towns, operated detention camps for non-Serbs and enemy soldiers, and systematically killed prisoners. Former UN rights chief Zeid Ra'ad al Hussein described him as "the epitome of evil" after his conviction. "This is all lies, you are all liars," he shouted when he was sentenced to life in prison in 2017. On Monday, Serbia's justice minister, Nenad Vujic, asked for Mladic to be transferred to a Belgrade military hospital, warning that his death "could come at any time." Born in Bosnia in 1942, Mladic was a former Yugoslav army officer who rose to command the Bosnian Serb army during the 1992-95 war.

stories.title: Tunisia mourns deceased migrants after small boat tragedy
stories.summary: Residents of a remote Tunisian city near the Libyan border attended the funeral of eight local youths who died in the Mediterranean. The tragedy took place late last week when a small boat carrying 15 people capsized near the Tunisian coastline.

stories.title: US holding off on returning to talks with Iran — White House
stories.summary: Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said "this will continue until the president feels that maybe they come to the table in a meaningful way"
article_sentences: NEW YORK, August 27.
The administration of US President Donald Trump is not yet holding talks with Iran on a peaceful resolution to the conflict, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said.
"No negotiations are happening right now, and this will continue until the president feels that maybe they come to the table in a meaningful way.
We have not seen that yet," she told Fox News.
Leavitt added that Trump has the final say on whether to resume the talks.

stories.title: Ghana bars export of unrefined gold
stories.summary: Ghana has announced a ban on the exporting of unrefined gold from the country. Africa’s leading gold producer wants to move beyond the role of a supplier of raw minerals and enable the country to capture greater economic value from its gold resources. Our correspondent, Justice Baidoo, has more.

stories.title: Russian Film Festival opens in five Chinese cities
stories.summary: The program includes Russian premieres, historical dramas, family films, and animated endeavors
article_sentences: BEIJING, August 27.
The Russian Film Festival has opened in five Chinese cities with the solemn ceremony taking place at the China Film Archive, a TASS correspondent reports.
Besides Beijing, Russian films will be shown in Shanghai, Hohhot, Harbin, and Heihe.
The program includes Russian premieres, historical dramas, family films, and animated endeavors.

Notable movies include war dramas "August" (2025), "Angels of Ladoga" (2026), "Litvyak" (2026) and "Father" (2026), as well as family films aimed at young audiences: "Cheburashka 2" (2026), "Buratino" (2026) and "Leo and Tig.
Road to Lake Baikal" (2026).
The screenings will take place from August 27 to September 2.

The Russian Film Festival is organized by Roskino together with the Chinese Center for Film Art Research, with the support of the Russian Culture Ministry and the State Administration of the People's Republic of China for Cinema.
The festival is being held in tandem with a large·scale Chinese Film Festival, which took place from June 8 to June 14 in Moscow, Yekaterinburg, and Vladivostok.

stories.title: OSCE/ODIHR not invited to monitor State Duma elections — diplomat
stories.summary: The ODIHR has established itself as a tool of hypocrisy, Maria Zakharova said
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 27.

The Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE/ODIHR), which has established itself as a tool of hypocrisy, will not participate in monitoring the upcoming State Duma elections in September, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said on Thursday.
"I believe that the ODIHR will go down as a structure famous for its double standards as an international elections overseer," she said.
"We have already said that it is exactly because of these reasons that it will not participate in international monitoring of the September elections in Russia."

"I would like to emphasize that our country, in accordance with the Copenhagen Document of 1990, completely fulfills its obligations by having invited a number of international organizations and structures, as well as individual OSCE countries, to observe [the election process]," Zakharova noted.
"We continue to advocate for the joint development of universal standards for observing international elections," she continued.

"However, in the current climate of rampant Russophobia in Western countries there is unfortunately no need to talk about any dialogue with them, including in the electoral sphere," Zakharova concluded.
Elections for State Duma lawmakers in the ninth convocation will be held from September 18-20, 2026.
